what: Redraws the image as copperplate engraving horizontal lines — shading becomes line thickness (darker is thicker, 3px spacing, grain slightly wavy) so it looks like a print, and each line (3px) is dragged sideways at random (drag = progress² × .9) While erased, scrubbing the screen from 94% → 66% (scrub .4) makes the lines return to place one by one and settle. With dust, it breaks into pieces at a noise threshold and drifts off to the upper right (WebGL2)

options.on: scroll (default — on scrubbing) · load (dur seconds right after attach)
options.dust: Degree of scattering into powder (0~1), default 0
options.ink: Name of the skin variable for line color, default --kf-ink (--kf-bg on a dark board)

from.where: index.js art() — ‹We are a brand agency› pistol·map, ‹What we offer› powder keg, footer powder keg (original cf-glfx canvas: ScrollTrigger top 94% → top 66%, scrub .4)

note: The image pixels are read into a texture, so only images or canvases from the same origin (or with CORS allowed) work. If the image background is transparent only the figure becomes a print, and with a white background the white areas have no lines (the brighter, the thinner the line)
